The '''Allen Institute for AI''' (abbreviated '''Ai2''') is a [[501(c)(3) organization|501(c)(3) non-profit]] scientific research institute founded by late [[Microsoft]] co-founder and philanthropist [[Paul Allen]] in 2014. The institute seeks to conduct high-impact AI research and engineering in service of the common good.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About — Allen Institute for AI |url=https://allenai.org/about |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=allenai.org |language=en}}</ref> Ai2 is based in [[Seattle]], and also has an active office in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Year in Review |url=https://allenai.org/newsletters/archive/2019-12-newsletter.html |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=allenai.org |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
[[Oren Etzioni]] was appointed by Paul Allen in September 2013 to direct the research at the institute.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cook |first=John |date=2013-09-04 |title=Going beyond Siri and Watson: Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen taps Oren Etzioni to lead new Artificial Intelligence Institute |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2013/microsoft-cofounder-paul-allen-taps-search-expert-oren-etzioni-lead-artificial-intelligence-institute/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=GeekWire}}</ref> After leading the organization for nine years, Etzioni stepped down from his role as CEO on September 30, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schlosser |first=Kurt |date=2022-06-15 |title=Oren Etzioni stepping down as CEO of Allen Institute for AI after nine years at research hub |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2022/oren-etzioni-stepping-down-as-ceo-of-allen-institute-for-ai-after-nine-years-at-research-hub/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=GeekWire}}</ref>  He was replaced in an interim capacity by the leading researcher of the company's Aristo project, Peter Clark.<ref name="Bishop-2023" /> On June 20, 2023, Ai2 announced [[Ali Farhadi]] as its next CEO starting July 31, 2023.<ref name="Bishop-2023">{{Cite news |last=Bishop |first=Todd |date=2023-06-20 |title=Apple machine learning leader Ali Farhadi named CEO of Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence |work=[[GeekWire]] |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2023/apple-machine-learning-leader-ali-farhadi-named-ceo-of-allen-institute-for-artificial-intelligence/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620203114/https://www.geekwire.com/2023/apple-machine-learning-leader-ali-farhadi-named-ceo-of-allen-institute-for-artificial-intelligence/ |archive-date=2023-06-20}}</ref> On March 10, 2026, Ai2 announced that Ali Farhadi would be stepping down as CEO after 2.5 years in the role, to be replaced by Peter Clark, again in an interim capacity.<ref name="Bishop-2026">{{Cite news |last=Bishop |first=Todd |date=2026-03-12 |title=Allen Institute for AI CEO Ali Farhadi steps down as nonprofit navigates shifting AI landscape |work=[[GeekWire]] |url=https://www.geekwire.com/2026/allen-institute-for-ai-ceo-ali-farhadi-steps-down-as-nonprofit-navigates-shifting-ai-landscape/}}</ref>

==Teams==
*'''Aristo''': Aristo is a flagship project of Ai2. Its original project goal was to design an artificially intelligent system that could successfully read, learn, and reason from texts and ultimately demonstrate its knowledge by successfully passing an 8th-grade science exam – the team achieved this objective in 2018. It was inspired by a similar project called Project Halo carried out by Seattle-based investment company Vulcan.<ref name="allenai-aristo">{{Cite web |title=Aristo — Allen Institute for AI |url=https://allenai.org/aristo |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=allenai.org |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>  The current focus of the team is to build the next generation of systems that can systematically reason, explain, and continually improve over time.<ref name="allenai-aristo"/>
*'''PRIOR''': The PRIOR team seeks to advance the field of computer vision by creating AI systems that can see, explore, learn, and reason about the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PRIOR |url=https://prior.allenai.org/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=prior.allenai.org |language=en-us}}</ref> The team released the open embodied AI platform AI2-THOR in 2016, supporting the training of AI agents in simulated environments.<ref>{{Cite web |publisher=Allen Institute for AI |title=AI2-THOR |url=https://ai2thor.allenai.org/ |access-date=2023-05-26}}</ref> In February 2018, the team released the game [[Iconary]] as a demonstration of an AI that can understand and produce situated scenes from a limited set of icons.
*'''[[Semantic Scholar]]''': Semantic Scholar tool is an [[Artificial intelligence|artificial-intelligence]] backed [[search engine]] for [[academic publications]] publicly released in November 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Jesus |date=2021-07-08 |title=🔹🔸Edge#104: AllenNLP Makes Cutting-Edge NLP Models Look Easy |url=https://thesequence.substack.com/p/edge104 |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=TheSequence}}</ref> It uses advances in [[natural language processing]] to provide features such as summaries for scholarly papers, contextual information about inline citations, and the ability to create libraries of papers and receive paper recommendations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Semantic Scholar {{!}} Product |url=https://www.semanticscholar.org/product |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=www.semanticscholar.org |language=en}}</ref>
*'''AllenNLP''': The AllenNLP team works on research to improve [[Neuro-linguistic programming|NLP]] systems' performance and accountability, and advance scientific methodologies for evaluating and understanding NLP systems. The team produces its own research as well as open-source tools to accelerate NLP research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AllenNLP — Allen Institute for AI |url=https://allenai.org/allennlp |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=allenai.org |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
*'''MOSAIC''': The Mosaic project is focused on defining and building [[Commonsense knowledge (artificial intelligence)|common sense knowledge]] and reasoning for AI systems.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dormehl |first=Luke |date=2018-04-13 |title=Forget Cloning, A.I. is the Real Way to Let Your Family Pooch Live Forever |url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/cool-tech/ai-behaves-like-dogs/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Digital Trends |language=en}}</ref>
*'''AI for the Environment''': These teams seek to apply artificial intelligence solutions to the prevention of poaching and illegal fishing in locations around the world, as well as environmental problems like climate modeling and wildfire management. The teams in this group include EarthRanger, Skylight, Climate Modeling, and Wildlands.

==Generative AI==

Ai2 has been actively involved in the development of [[open-source artificial intelligence]] through the release of fully open [[large language models]], datasets, and model training assets.

=== Olmo model family ===
On May 11, 2023, Ai2 announced they were developing OLMo, an open language model aiming to match the performance of other state-of-the-art language models.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Groeneveld |first1=Dirk |title=OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models |date=2024 |eprint=2402.00838 |last2=Beltagy |first2=Iz |last3=Walsh |first3=Pete |last4=Bhagia |first4=Akshita |last5=Kinney |first5=Rodney |last6=Tafjord |first6=Oyvind |last7=Jha |first7=Ananya Harsh |last8=Ivison |first8=Hamish |last9=Magnusson |first9=Ian |class=cs.CL }}</ref> In February 2024, 1B and 7B parameter variants of the model were open-sourced, including code, model weights with intermediate snapshots and logs, and contents of their Dolma training dataset (a three-trillion-token English corpus drawn from web text, academic publications, code, books, social media, and encyclopedic sources),<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Soldaini |first1=Luca |title=Dolma: an Open Corpus of Three Trillion Tokens for Language Model Pretraining Research |date=2024 |eprint=2402.00159 |last2=Kinney |first2=Rodney |last3=Bhagia |first3=Akshita |last4=Schwenk |first4=Dustin |last5=Atkinson |first5=David |last6=Authur |first6=Russell |last7=Bogin |first7=Ben |last8=Chandu |first8=Khyathi |last9=Dumas |first9=Jennifer |class=cs.CL }}</ref> making it the most open state-of-the-art model available.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-18 |title=Announcing AI2 OLMo, an open language model made by scientists, for scientists |url=https://blog.allenai.org/announcing-ai2-olmo-an-open-language-model-made-by-scientists-for-scientists-ab761e4e9b76 |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Medium |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiggers |first=Kyle |date=2024-02-01 |title=AI2 open sources text-generating AI models -- and the data used to train them |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/02/01/ai2-open-sources-text-generating-ai-models-and-the-data-used-to-train-them/ |access-date=2024-02-03 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

In September 2024, Ai2 released OLMoE, the first [[mixture of experts|mixture-of-experts]] model in the OLMo family, developed jointly with Contextual AI. The sparse model has roughly 7 billion total parameters, of which about 1 billion are active per input token, and was trained on 5 trillion tokens. As with other OLMo releases, the model weights were accompanied by the training data, code, logs, and intermediate training checkpoints.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Muennighoff |first1=Niklas |last2=Soldaini |first2=Luca |last3=Groeneveld |first3=Dirk |last4=Lo |first4=Kyle |last5=Morrison |first5=Jacob |last6=Min |first6=Sewon |last7=Shi |first7=Weijia |last8=Walsh |first8=Pete |last9=Tafjord |first9=Oyvind |year=2024 |title=OLMoE: Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models |eprint=2409.02060 |class=cs.CL}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=OLMoE: An open, small, and state-of-the-art mixture-of-experts model |url=https://allenai.org/blog/olmoe-an-open-small-and-state-of-the-art-mixture-of-experts-model-c258432d0514 |website=allenai.org |access-date=2026-07-24}}</ref>

In November 2024, Ai2 released the second iteration of Olmo, OLMo 2, with the initial release including 7B and 13B parameter models.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OLMo 2: The best fully open language model to date {{!}} Ai2 |url=https://allenai.org/blog/olmo2 |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=allenai.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=OLMo |first1=Team |title=2 OLMo 2 Furious |date=2025 |eprint=2501.00656 |last2=Walsh |first2=Pete |last3=Soldaini |first3=Luca |last4=Groeneveld |first4=Dirk |last5=Lo |first5=Kyle |last6=Arora |first6=Shane |last7=Bhagia |first7=Akshita |last8=Gu |first8=Yuling |last9=Huang |first9=Shengyi |class=cs.CL }}</ref> In March 2025, Ai2 released a 32B variant of OLMo 2, claiming to have released "the first fully-open model (all data, code, weights, and details are freely available) to outperform GPT3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o mini".<ref>{{Cite web |title=OLMo 2 32B: First fully open model to outperform GPT 3.5 and GPT 4o mini {{!}} Ai2 |url=https://allenai.org/blog/olmo2-32b |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=allenai.org |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2025, Ai2 released their Olmo 3 set of models (now styled with a lowercase "L" and "M"). These included the Olmo 3 Think (7 and 32B), Olmo 3 Base (7 and 32B), Olmo 3 Instruct (7B) and Olmo 3 RL Zero (7B).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olmo 3: Charting a path through the model flow to lead open-source AI {{!}} Ai2 |url=https://allenai.org/blog/olmo3 |access-date=2025-11-24 |website=allenai.org |language=en}}</ref> In December 2025, Ai2 announced an update to the 32B model, Olmo 3.1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=David |first=Emilia |title=Ai2's new Olmo 3.1 extends reinforcement learning training for stronger reasoning benchmarks |url=https://venturebeat.com/ai/ai2s-new-olmo-3-1-extends-reinforcement-learning-training-for-stronger}}</ref>

=== Tulu models and post-training recipes ===
In addition to the fully-open Olmo family of models, Ai2 has also developed Tulu, a family of instruction-tuned models and open post-training recipes that build on open-weights base models (e.g., Meta's Llama) to provide fully transparent alternatives to proprietary instruction-tuning methods.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coldewey |first=Devin |date=2024-11-21 |title=Ai2's open source Tülu 3 lets anyone play the AI post-training game |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/11/21/ai2s-open-source-tulu-3-lets-anyone-play-the-ai-post-training-game/ |access-date=2025-08-26 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> AI2 released the first iteration of Tulu in June 2023,<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Wang |first1=Yizhong |title=How Far Can Camels Go? Exploring the State of Instruction Tuning on Open Resources |date=2023 |eprint=2306.04751 |last2=Ivison |first2=Hamish |last3=Dasigi |first3=Pradeep |last4=Hessel |first4=Jack |last5=Khot |first5=Tushar |last6=Chandu |first6=Khyathi Raghavi |last7=Wadden |first7=David |last8=MacMillan |first8=Kelsey |last9=Smith |first9=Noah A. |class=cs.CL }}</ref> with subsequent iterations being released in November 2023 (Tulu 2<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Ivison |first1=Hamish |title=Camels in a Changing Climate: Enhancing LM Adaptation with Tulu 2 |eprint=2311.10702 |last2=Wang |first2=Yizhong |last3=Pyatkin |first3=Valentina |last4=Lambert |first4=Nathan |last5=Peters |first5=Matthew |last6=Dasigi |first6=Pradeep |last7=Jang |first7=Joel |last8=Wadden |first8=David |last9=Smith |first9=Noah A. |date=2023 |class=cs.CL }}</ref>) and November 2024 (Tulu 3<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Lambert |first1=Nathan |title=Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training |date=2025-04-14 |eprint=2411.15124 |last2=Morrison |first2=Jacob |last3=Pyatkin |first3=Valentina |last4=Huang |first4=Shengyi |last5=Ivison |first5=Hamish |last6=Brahman |first6=Faeze |last7=Miranda |first7=Lester James V. |last8=Liu |first8=Alisa |last9=Dziri |first9=Nouha |class=cs.CL }}</ref>).
